stem: Name this bone. The bone shown here is the ___.
explanation: The arrow points to the scaphoid, a carpal (wrist) bone on the thumb side of the proximal row. It is the most commonly fractured carpal bone.

stem: Name this structure. The structure shown here is the ___.
correct: arrector pili|arrector pili muscle|arrector pili muscles
explanation: The small red band of smooth muscle attached to the hair follicle is the arrector pili. When it contracts it pulls the hair upright (goose bumps).

stem: Name the skin type. The skin type shown here is ___.
explanation: This is thin skin: a thin epidermis with many hair follicles. Thick skin (palms and soles) has a thick stratum corneum and no hair.

topic: Bones of the skull and neck
stem: Name this bone. The bone shown here is the ___.
explanation: This U-shaped bone is the hyoid. It sits in the neck below the mandible and is the only bone that does not join any other bone.

stem: Name this structure. The structure shown here is the ___.
correct: pacinian corpuscle|pacinian corpuscles|pacinian|lamellated corpuscle|lamellated corpuscles|pacinian (lamellated) corpuscle
explanation: The large oval receptor deep in the dermis is a Pacinian (lamellated) corpuscle. It senses deep pressure and vibration.

stem: Name this bone. The bone shown here is the ___.
explanation: The arrow points to the broad, flared ilium, the largest and top part of the hip (coxal) bone.

stem: Name this bone. The bone shown here is the ___.
explanation: This is the tibia (shinbone). Its wide, flat top forms the knee joint with the femur, and it is much thicker than the fibula.

stem: Name this structure. The structure shown here is the ___.
explanation: The arrow points to the hair follicle, the tube of epidermal cells that surrounds the hair root in the dermis.

stem: Name this structure. The structure shown here is the ___.
correct: meissner's corpuscle|meissners corpuscle|meissner corpuscle|meissner's corpuscles|meissners corpuscles|tactile corpuscle|tactile corpuscles|meissner’s corpuscle
explanation: This is a Meissner's (tactile) corpuscle, a light-touch receptor in a dermal papilla just under the epidermis.

stem: Name this phase. The phase shown here is ___.
explanation: The arrow points to a cell whose chromosomes are being pulled apart toward opposite ends of the cell: anaphase.

stem: Name this structure. This group of bones is called ___.
explanation: The arrow points to the sacrum, five fused sacral vertebrae that join the two hip bones at the back of the pelvis.

stem: Name this structure. The structure shown here is the ___.
correct: anterior fontanel|anterior fontanelle|anterior fontanels|anterior fontanelles|frontal fontanel|frontal fontanelle
explanation: This diamond-shaped soft spot on the fetal skull is the anterior fontanel, where the frontal and parietal bones meet. It closes by about 18 to 24 months.

stem: Name the "black" structure. The structure shown here is a(n) ___.
explanation: The small dark spaces in rings around the central canal hold osteocytes, mature bone cells, each sitting in a lacuna.

stem: Name the red structure. The structure shown in red is the ___.
correct: styloid process|styloid|styloid process of the temporal bone
explanation: The thin, pointed red projection below the ear is the styloid process of the temporal bone. Muscles of the tongue and neck attach to it.

stem: Name the phase. The phase shown here is ___.
explanation: The arrow points to a cell with an intact nucleus and no visible chromosomes. The cell is in interphase, not yet dividing.

stem: Name this bone. The bone shown here is the ___.
explanation: This is the ulna. The hook-shaped end (the olecranon and trochlear notch) forms the elbow with the humerus.

stem: Name the layer. This layer is the ___.
explanation: The arrow points to the stratum spinosum, the thick layer of the epidermis above the stratum basale where cells are joined by desmosomes.

stem: Name this "line". This "line" is called the ___.
explanation: The line running front to back along the top of the skull, between the two parietal bones, is the sagittal suture.

stem: Name this bone. The bone shown here is the ___.
explanation: This long, thin bone is the fibula, the lateral bone of the lower leg. It is much thinner than the tibia and does not carry much weight.

stem: Name this bone. The bone shown here is the ___.
explanation: This is the humerus, the upper arm bone. The round head fits into the scapula at the shoulder.

stem: Name this structure. The structure shown here is the ___.
explanation: The arrow points to the vomer, the thin bone that forms the lower part of the nasal septum.

stem: Name the structure. The arrow is pointing to the ___.
correct: central canal|haversian canal|central (haversian) canal|central canal (haversian canal)|haversian
explanation: The dark hole in the center of the osteon is the central (Haversian) canal, which carries blood vessels and nerves through compact bone.

stem: Name this landmark. This "landmark" is called the ___.
explanation: The red saddle-shaped dip in the sphenoid bone is the sella turcica (Turkish saddle). The pituitary gland sits in it.

stem: Name the phase. The phase shown here is ___.
explanation: The arrow points to a cell with two separate clusters of chromosomes at opposite ends and a new cell wall forming between them: telophase.

stem: Name the light purple bone. The bone shown here is the ___.
explanation: The light purple bone is the zygomatic bone, the cheekbone. It forms part of the eye socket and the zygomatic arch.

stem: Name this bone. The bone shown here is the ___.
explanation: This is the mandible, the lower jaw. It is the only movable bone of the skull.

stem: Name this bone feature. The structure shown here is the ___.
explanation: The deep cup on the side of the hip bone is the acetabulum. The head of the femur fits into it to form the hip joint.

stem: Name this structure. The bone shown here is the ___.
correct: medial cuboid bone|medial cuboid|medial cuneiform|medial cuneiform bone|first cuneiform
explanation: The arrow points to the medial cuneiform, the tarsal bone on the big-toe side just behind the first metatarsal.

stem: Name this structure. The structure shown here is the ___.
explanation: The small, pointed tip at the bottom of the sternum is the xiphoid process.

stem: Name this group of bones. The group of bones shown here are the ___.
explanation: The arrow points to the thoracic vertebrae, the 12 vertebrae in the middle of the spine where the ribs attach.

stem: Name the red "line". The "red line" is the ___.
explanation: The red line at the back of the skull is the lambdoid suture, where the parietal bones meet the occipital bone.

stem: Name the structure. The structure shown here is ___.
correct: meissner's corpuscle|meissners corpuscle|meissner corpuscle|meissner's corpuscles|meissners corpuscles|tactile corpuscle|tactile corpuscles|a meissner's corpuscle|meissner’s corpuscle
explanation: This is a Meissner's (tactile) corpuscle, a light-touch receptor in a dermal papilla just under the epidermis.

stem: Name the process. The process shown here is the ___.
correct: mastoid process|mastoid|mastoid process of the temporal bone
explanation: The arrow points to the mastoid process of the temporal bone, just behind the ear. Neck muscles such as the sternocleidomastoid attach to it.

stem: Name the "hole". The hole shown here is the ___.
explanation: The large hole in the base of the skull (occipital bone) is the foramen magnum. The spinal cord passes through it.

stem: Name this group of bones. This group of bones are called the ___.
explanation: The arrow points to the metatarsals, the five long bones of the foot between the tarsals and the toes.

stem: Name this phase. The phase shown here is ___.
explanation: The arrow points to a cell whose two sets of chromosomes are moving apart toward opposite poles: anaphase.

stem: Name this bone. The bone shown here is the ___.
explanation: The arrow points to the capitate, the largest carpal bone, in the middle of the distal row of the wrist.

stem: Name the bone. The bone shown here is the ___.
explanation: The arrow points to the brown temporal bone on the side of the skull around the ear.

stem: Name this bone. This bone is the ___.
explanation: This small, flat, rounded bone is the patella (kneecap), a sesamoid bone in the quadriceps tendon.

stem: Name the skin type. The skin type shown here is ___.
explanation: This is thick skin: a very thick stratum corneum and a stratum lucidum, found on the palms and soles.

stem: Name these bones. The bones shown here are the ___.
explanation: These are femurs, the thigh bones, the longest and strongest bones in the body.

stem: Name the bone in green. The bone highlighted in green is the ___.
explanation: The green bat-shaped bone is the sphenoid, which spans the middle of the skull's base and touches every other cranial bone.

stem: Name this bone. The bone shown here is the ___.
explanation: The arrow points to the navicular, a tarsal bone on the medial side of the foot between the talus and the cuneiforms.

stem: Name the structure. The structure shown here is the ___.
explanation: This is a sebaceous (oil) gland beside the hair follicle. It secretes sebum into the follicle to soften hair and skin.

stem: Name the brown structure. The brown structure shown here is the ___.
correct: hair root|root of the hair|hair roots
explanation: The brown structure below the skin's surface is the hair root, sitting inside the hair follicle. The part above the surface is the hair shaft.

stem: Name the phase this cell is in. The phase shown here is ___.
explanation: The chromosomes are lined up in a single row across the middle of the cell, so the cell is in metaphase.

stem: Name this layer. The layer shown here is the ___.
explanation: The arrow points to the stratum corneum, the outermost layer of the epidermis, made of flat, dead, keratin-filled cells.

stem: Name the bone. The bone shown here is the ___.
explanation: The arrow points to the calcaneus, the heel bone and the largest tarsal bone. The Achilles tendon attaches to it.

stem: Name this bone. The bone shown here is the ___.
explanation: The arrow points to the sternum (breastbone), the flat bone in the middle of the chest where the ribs attach in front.

stem: Name this bone. The bone shown here is the ___.
explanation: This is the axis (C2). The upward peg, the dens, is the pivot the atlas turns on when you shake your head "no."
